## Goal

Introduce one persistent native on or off control that governs the private evidence IPC service and makes disabled access explicit without affecting monitoring or stored evidence.

## Deliverables

- Persistent Agent Access setting
- IPC lifecycle controller
- Native MCP access toggle and status
- Disabled-state helper guidance
- Privacy-boundary tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-230-01` — A fresh install defaults Agent Access off; the user can enable or disable it with a native toggle, and the choice persists across app relaunches.
- `AC-230-02` — Enabling Agent Access starts the owner-only Unix socket and permits the existing read-only MCP queries; disabling it closes active service availability, removes the socket, and causes the helper to return clear disabled-by-user guidance.
- `AC-230-03` — Changing Agent Access never pauses monitoring, deletes or rewrites evidence, modifies Codex or Claude configuration, expands MCP beyond read-only tools, or opens a network listener.
- `AC-230-04` — The control exposes on, off, starting, and degraded states without relying on color alone and remains synchronized anywhere its status is presented.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-230-01` (privacy-boundary-test) — Fresh-install default, persistence, service start and stop, socket removal, disabled helper response, active query, monitoring independence, and accessibility state results.
